Luke 21:1–4 — the widow’s two small coins are valued because she gives out of poverty."],"prominence":"common"},{"meaning":"Betrayal, corrupt payment, or blood money.","basis":["Matthew 26:14–16; 27:3–10 — the thirty pieces of silver paid for Jesus’ betrayal.","Zechariah 11:12–13 — the thirty pieces of silver provide the prophetic background used by Matthew."],"prominence":"common"},{"meaning":"Humanity bearing the divine image and recovered through salvation; in detailed allegorical readings, the woman searching for the coin represents God, divine Wisdom, or the Church.","basis":["Luke 15:8–10 — developed allegorically from the lost coin’s retained value and recoverability.","Genesis 1:26–27 — invoked because a coin bears an image, analogously to humanity bearing God’s image."],"prominence":"minority"}],"has_settled_consensus":false,"confidence":"high","notes":"There is no settled, universal biblical symbolism of the coin.
